messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service `auth-service` — symptom: jwt_verif_error_rate > 3% (5m). Priority: P2. Paging #incidents and @eng-oncall. Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC123456

PagerDuty: Incident INC123456 created by monitoring (jwt-verifier). Escalation policy: auth-oncall -> eng-oncall. Details: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/INC123456

Alice Ramos: acked oncall via PagerDuty — I'm on it, looking at logs now.

Ben Chu: taking lead. quick question — customer impact? rough numbers?

Customer Success Bot: CS alert: spike in 401s correlated with incoming token validation failures. ~12 support tickets opened, top affected tenant: acme-corp (10% of their requests return 401).

Ben Chu: grep from verifier logs shows lots of `kid not found` errors. Example: `ERROR jwt_verifier: kid abc123 not present in JWKS` repeating across multiple pods.

Alice Ramos: quick check — curl to JWKS endpoint from a healthy pod:
```
curl -s https://auth-public.example/.well-known/jwks.json | jq '.keys[].kid'
"def456","ghi789"
```
But tokens are signed with `abc123`. jwks.json doesn't include `abc123`.

Evelyn (SRE): looks like JWKS propagation failed after recent key rotation. Also note our `auth-cache-service` sets Cache-Control: max-age=300 by default. Could be stale caches.

Ben Chu: timeline: signer v2.1 rolled ~20m ago and key-rotation job ran. Verifier pods in some AZs still have cached JWKS that don't include the new kid.

Alice Ramos: mitigation options:
1) force JWKS cache invalidation on verifiers (admin endpoint)
2) temporarily configure verifiers to consult remote JWKS for misses (failover)
3) if needed, roll back signer to previous key set

Ben Chu: performing step 1 — hitting internal admin endpoint to clear caches:
```
curl -X POST https://auth.internal/admin/clear-jwks -H 'Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>' -d '{}' -v
> HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

incident-bot: Action logged — `clear-jwks` invoked by Ben Chu. Affected pods: auth-verifier-0, auth-verifier-4, auth-verifier-7 (us-east-1b).

Customer Success Bot: after cache clear, 401 rate for acme-corp dropped from 4.5% -> 0.9% within 6 minutes. Monitoring: https://grafana.example/d/abc123/jwt-metrics

Alice Ramos: still seeing two stuck pods that didn't pick up new JWKS. I'm going to restart those verifier pods to force a fetch. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/auth-verifier -n prod --selector=zone=us-east-1b`

Charlie Kim: I'll take the restart. initiating now — restarting pod auth-verifier-4 and auth-verifier-7.

Charlie Kim: restarts completed. Logs show successful JWKS fetch and messages `INFO jwt_verifier: matched kid abc123, validation successful`

Ben Chu: confirming token verification error rate back to baseline (~0.1%). Customer impact appears mitigated.

Alice Ramos: marking incident as mitigated. Next: post-incident tasks — RCA and followups. Preliminary hypothesis: key-propagation job posted new key to config-store but the verifier cache invalidation didn't fire for a subset of pods due to a race with the deployment rollout and cache TTL.

Ben Chu: proposed follow-ups:
- create end-to-end pre-rollout check that verifies JWKS contains new kid across at least 95% of verifier pods
- add a post-rotation hook to explicitly call /admin/clear-jwks on verifiers
- improve observability: alert when `kid` mismatch > 0.5% for 3m

Customer Success Bot: CS communication drafted and queued for release to affected tenants. ETA 30m.

incident-bot: No further escalations. Please confirm when you want PagerDuty incident closed.

PagerDuty: Incident INC123456 acknowledged by Alice Ramos at 3601234599. Please close when postmortem ticket exists.

Alice Ramos: closing loop for now. Handoff: Charlie Kim will own postmortem and follow-ups during his shift. Tagging #postmortems and #eng-infra for the RCA. :white_check_mark:

Charlie Kim: got it — I'll file the postmortem, include timeline and a rollback playbook, and assign tickets to infra + deploy teams. Will update here when done.

Ben Chu: thanks everyone for the quick response. Leaving monitoring on watch for 2 hours.
